function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

**How Turbonomics Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability** | Aspect | What Turbonomics Brings | How It Differs from Native Cloud Observability | |--------|------------------------|----------------------------------------------| | **Unified Visibility Across Clouds** | • Aggregates telemetry from all clouds (AWS, Azure, GCP) into a single pane.
• Normalizes metrics (CPU, memory, I/O, network, cost) so they’re comparable across providers. | Native tools (CloudWatch, Stackdriver, Monitor) provide visibility *within* each provider but require separate dashboards, APIs, and alerting rules. | | **AI‑Driven Root Cause Analysis** | • Uses machine learning models to correlate performance anomalies with underlying causes (e.g., resource contention, mis‑configured autoscaling).
• Provides automated diagnostic workflows that span multiple clouds. | Native tools rely on rule‑based alerts or manual log correlation; they lack cross‑cloud ML diagnostics. | | **Predictive Capacity Planning** | • Forecasts future demand and capacity needs using time‑series forecasting models.
• Recommends right‑size resources before bottlenecks occur. | Native tools offer historical trend charts and simple forecasting (e.g., CloudWatch Alarms), but not predictive recommendations that span heterogeneous workloads. | | **Cost Optimization & Chargeback** | • Calculates real‑time cost per workload, attributing spend to business units or product lines.
• Suggests cost‑saving actions (rightsizing, spot instances, reserved capacity). | Native cost tools (Cost Explorer, Budgets) show spend but don’t tie it to performance or automatically recommend actions across clouds. | | **Policy‑Based Automation** | • Implements policies that automatically scale, migrate, or terminate workloads based on business SLAs and cost thresholds.
• Supports “policy as code” that can be versioned and audited. | Native tools expose scaling policies but require separate configuration per provider; they don’t enforce unified policy compliance across clouds. | | **Security & Compliance Context** | • Adds security metadata (vulnerability scores, compliance checks) to performance data, enabling risk‑aware decision making. | Native security services (GuardDuty, Security Center, Cloud Security Command Center) operate independently of performance data. | ### Practical Impact for Unilever 1. **Single Source of Truth** – All performance, cost, and security data appear in one dashboard, reducing the cognitive load on platform teams. 2. **Cross‑Cloud Optimization** – AI identifies where workloads should live (e.g., compute‑intensive vs. memory‑intensive) and automatically migrates them to the most cost‑effective region/provider. 3. **Business‑Aligned Decision Making** – By tying cost and performance to product lines, Unilever can see the true ROI of digital initiatives and justify budget allocations. 4. **Reduced Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR)** – Automated root‑cause analysis cuts investigation time from hours to minutes, freeing engineers to focus on innovation. --- **Key Differences Between Turbonomics and Native Cloud Observability Tools** | Feature | Turbonomics | Native Cloud Observability (GCP, AWS, Azure) | |---------|-------------|---------------------------------------------| | **Scope** | Cross‑cloud, multi‑tenant | Single‑cloud, provider‑specific | | **Data Normalization** | Yes (metrics, logs, cost) | No (each provider uses its own schema) | | **AI/ML Capabilities** | Predictive analytics, anomaly detection, recommendation engine | Mostly rule‑based alerts, limited ML | | **Automation** | Policy‑driven auto‑remediation, auto‑migration | Manual scaling policies, separate automation scripts | | **Cost Attribution** | Real‑time cost per workload, chargeback | Cost reports at account/project level | | **Integration** | Works with Kubernetes, OpenShift, VMs, containers, serverless | Limited to provider’s ecosystem | | **Governance** | Unified policy enforcement, audit trails | Provider‑level governance only | In short, Turbonomics extends beyond what native observability offers by providing a unified, AI‑powered layer that spans all of Unilever’s cloud environments, turning raw telemetry into actionable insights that drive both performance and cost efficiency.
